title: The Hard Border
premise: Beatrix Brightwater, a private security contractor whose clients pay for deniability, is hired to quietly investigate the disappearance of Flight 447's records while the plane was still airborne. Following corrupted manifests and erased crew files, she uncovers a smuggling network run by border officials who plan to detonate a cargo of stolen ordnance at the Meridian checkpoint, timed to look like an accident during shift change. Betrayed by her own employer and haunted by gaps in her memory from an earlier contract gone wrong, Beatrix assembles a makeshift team of discarded operatives who become the family she never had. In the final hours, she exposes the conspiracy, stops the blast, and chooses to testify publicly rather than stay invisible — burning her career to keep her found family alive.
about_author: E. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing risk assessments for firms that preferred their names left off paperwork. The Hard Border is their third thriller, drawn from years of watching what happens when accountability becomes optional.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Beatrix takes a low-profile retainer from an aviation insurer: find out why every digital trace of Flight 447 vanished mid-flight. POV: Beatrix. She works alone by habit, wary after a past contract left her with memory gaps. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking loneliness; the case feels like just another job nobody will admit to owning.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't on the Manifest
chapters.summary: A ground handler claims he loaded a crate that appears on no manifest, then disappears. Beatrix pulls airport security footage before it's wiped. POV: Beatrix, with a brief interlude from handler Tomas Okafor's last voicemail. Emotional beat: first real fear — someone is erasing people, not just records, and she may be next.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Beatrix maps the Meridian checkpoint's rotation and notices every anomaly clusters around one shift change window. Her employer, Corvane Security, orders her to drop it. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: suspicion curdles into certainty that her own firm is inside the circle; she begins keeping a second, private file.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Tracking the crate's route, Beatrix finds a dockworker who saw the transfer — and recognizes her own handwriting in an old incident report she has no memory of filing. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: dread turns inward; the conspiracy may have touched her past, and her missing memories become evidence she can't read.

chapters.title: Discards
chapters.summary: Beatrix recruits three burned operatives: ex-customs analyst Priya Raghavan, disgraced pilot Callum Voss, and quiet fixer Marek Dusek. POV: rotating among the four. Emotional beat: guarded strangers testing each other over bad coffee; the first fragile stitches of found family form around shared distrust of institutions.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya decodes a smuggled ledger tying checkpoint officials to Corvane executives; the 'accident' is scheduled for Thursday's shift change. POV: Priya, then Beatrix. Emotional beat: triumph at cracking the code immediately shadowed by horror at its scale — and the realization that going public means going to war.

chapters.title: Safe House Rules
chapters.summary: Corvane burns Beatrix's credentials and puts out a quiet kill order. The team holes up in Marek's safe house, trading stories they'd never tell employers. POV: Marek. Emotional beat: warmth under siege — the group stops being a crew and becomes a household, even as surveillance tightens outside.

chapters.title: Thursday, 05:40
chapters.summary: A mole inside the team's orbit tips off the conspirators; Callum is taken to force the ledger's return. POV: Callum under interrogation, intercut with Beatrix choosing rescue over the mission clock. Emotional beat: the family bond is tested against the deadline — saving him costs them their best window, and none of them regret it.

chapters.title: The Hard Border
chapters.summary: Climax: during shift change, Beatrix infiltrates the checkpoint, triggers the crate's failsafe lockout, and confronts Corvane's director — who reveals he authored the operation that took her memories. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: cold fury transmuted into resolve; she defeats him not with force but by broadcasting the evidence live, making secrecy impossible.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Resolution: arrests ripple through two agencies; Beatrix testifies on record, ending her anonymity-for-hire career. The team stays together, opening a small independent consultancy. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: quiet peace — she still can't recover her lost memories, but she no longer needs them to know who she is.
